question: Should OpenClaw pursue a backend-neutral distributed scheduler/job ownership contract in core or plugin APIs, document ScalyClaw/BullMQ-style orchestration as external only, or defer the broad work to the narrower cron/session/runtime trackers?
rationale: The missing source capability is clear, but backend boundary, config shape, worker failure semantics, credential handling, observability, and core-versus-plugin ownership require maintainer architecture intent.

options.title: Design Backend-Neutral Contract
options.body: Define shared queue/state, worker claiming, retries/backoff, dead-letter semantics, cron support, and observability before any Redis/BullMQ-specific code lands.

options.title: Split Into Narrow Tracks
options.body: Keep this issue as prior art while cron HA, external session storage, distributed runtime, and plugin/API issues each own their narrower implementation choices.

options.title: Document External Orchestration
options.body: Decide not to add a core backend for now and document safe external queue or scheduler patterns around OpenClaw deployments.

recommendation.title: Design Backend-Neutral Contract
recommendation.body: Define shared queue/state, worker claiming, retries/backoff, dead-letter semantics, cron support, and observability before any Redis/BullMQ-specific code lands.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete already routed this issue as architecture input and has the strongest queue/cron history in the checked surfaces.
